assumptions.statement: PostgreSQL 16 on Amazon RDS is the database engine.
assumptions.reason: You indicated a relational database; PostgreSQL is a widely supported default.

assumptions.statement: Application servers run Amazon Linux 2023 on Graviton (arm64) instances and Node.js listens on port 3000 behind the load balancer.
assumptions.reason: Lowest-cost general-purpose option, with the usual default port for your runtime; a placeholder app is installed until you deploy your own.

assumptions.reason: Avoids creating a state bucket; not suitable for teams or production.

architecture.name: Balanced
architecture.summary: Three-tier layout with private application servers, one NAT gateway and a Multi-AZ database.

components.label: Customers
components.rationale: Internet users reach the application only through the load balancer.

components.label: AWS account
components.rationale: Terraform refuses to run against any other account.

components.label: VPC 10.20.0.0/16
components.rationale: Private network with separate tiers per availability zone.

components.label: Public subnets (2 AZs)
components.rationale: Only components that must face the internet live here.

components.label: Private app subnets (2 AZs)
components.rationale: Servers are not directly reachable from the internet.

components.label: NAT gateway ×1

details.Purpose: outbound updates and AWS API calls

components.rationale: A single NAT keeps cost down; if its AZ fails, outbound traffic from servers stops.

components.label: Isolated data subnets (2 AZs)
components.rationale: The database has no path to or from the internet.

components.label: Application Load Balancer
components.rationale: Single public entry point; terminates TLS and spreads load across zones.

components.label: App servers (auto scaling)
components.rationale: Replaced automatically when unhealthy; scales on CPU.

components.label: Instance role

details.Grants: SSM Session Manager, read own DB secret

components.rationale: Temporary credentials with only the permissions the servers need.

components.label: SSM Session Manager
components.rationale: Administrative access without exposing ports to the internet.

components.label: RDS PostgreSQL 16
components.rationale: Managed PostgreSQL with automated backups and patching.

components.label: Secrets Manager
components.rationale: Credentials are generated and rotated by AWS, never stored in Terraform.

components.label: Uploads bucket (S3)
components.rationale: User files live outside the servers so they survive replacement and scaling.

components.label: Alerts (CloudWatch → email)

details.Alarms: 5xx errors, unhealthy servers, DB CPU, DB free storage

components.rationale: Your team hears about problems before customers do.

components.label: Log bucket (S3)
components.rationale: Private, tamper-resistant store for access, flow and audit logs.

components.label: CloudTrail
components.rationale: Records every AWS API call for auditing.

components.label: VPC flow logs
components.rationale: Network-level record of accepted and rejected connections.

decisions.title: Network tiers
decisions.choice: Public / private app / isolated data subnets
decisions.rationale: Each tier can only be reached from the tier in front of it.

decisions.title: Administrative access
decisions.rationale: No inbound administrative ports; sessions are authenticated with IAM and can be logged.

decisions.title: Workload identity
decisions.choice: EC2 instance role with SSM core policy and a tag-scoped secret read
decisions.rationale: Temporary credentials, no access keys on servers.

decisions.title: Encryption at rest
decisions.choice: AWS-managed keys for RDS, EBS and S3

decisions.title: Logging
decisions.choice: CloudTrail, VPC flow logs, ALB access logs
decisions.rationale: Delivered to one private bucket with 90-day retention.

decisions.title: Compute
decisions.choice: Auto scaling group of t4g.medium (2–6), scaling out above 60% CPU
decisions.rationale: Self-healing and elastic without container-platform complexity.
alternatives: ECS Fargate (no server management, higher unit cost)

decisions.title: Cost posture
decisions.rationale: See the cost breakdown and trade-offs.

decisions.title: Tagging
decisions.rationale: Every resource is attributable to this project.

decisions.title: TLS
decisions.choice: TLS 1.2+ at the load balancer, TLS enforced to the database
decisions.rationale: Encrypts every hop that crosses a network boundary.

decisions.title: Database placement
decisions.rationale: No route to or from the internet.

decisions.title: Database resilience
decisions.rationale: Multi-AZ fails over automatically in 1–2 minutes.

decisions.title: Database credentials
decisions.choice: RDS-managed master password in Secrets Manager
decisions.rationale: Credentials never touch Terraform state or the repository.

decisions.title: File storage
decisions.choice: Private S3 bucket with an IAM policy scoped to the app role
decisions.rationale: Durable, encrypted object storage that servers can be replaced around; never public.
alternatives: EFS shared file system (more expensive, POSIX semantics)

decisions.title: Alerting
decisions.choice: CloudWatch alarms → KMS-encrypted SNS topic → ops@example.com
decisions.rationale: A customer-managed key is used because CloudWatch cannot publish to topics encrypted with the AWS-managed SNS key.
alternatives: Third-party monitoring (Datadog, PagerDuty) via the same SNS topic
